decisions.reason: The dashboard-specific requirements in message 36 are already captured by the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE; streamlining the model interface adds no further dashboard-state change.
Making the interface easier to understand and audit does not change the existing rules for documenting assumptions, selecting sources, or handling unavailable inputs.
The source requests stronger presentation of debt performance and project-finance analysis but does not change the capital structure, financing rate, tranche structure, or refinement trigger.
Interface streamlining does not alter the capex estimate, assumption basis, included costs, or line-item treatment.
The source does not change the eight-site count, selected site list, or basis for modeling unavailable site-level information.
The request to streamline and clarify the model does not change the operating-cost range, source, or treatment of the appendix amount.
Requiring an understandable interface while retaining technical functionality does not modify the existing formula, worksheet-link, or output-credibility standards.
The source does not change the DSCR threshold, equity-IRR threshold, or availability-payment sizing method.
The interface simplification decision does not change the required Canadian CCA method, asset classes, or modeled tax effects.
The source reinforces communication of viability and bankability but does not change the existing user-funded and PPP scenarios or their required finding.
Streamlining the model interface does not alter source-data verification, primary reference sources, or the directional role of the demand analysis.
A simpler and more auditable interface does not necessarily alter the integrated three-statement structure or the financial-engine basis.
